quote.quote: The Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee was convened on November 6, 2014.
This application was presented to the ODAC on November 6, 2014.

recommendation.text: ODAC voted 2 Yes / 5 No (0 abstain) that the benefit of adding panobinostat to bortezomib and dexamethasone did not outweigh the risks for patients with relapsed multiple myeloma — i.e., a majority voted against the broad proposed indication.

linkages.concern: ODAC majority voted 'no', citing the drug's toxicity and the uncertain magnitude of the PFS improvement as yielding a negative overall benefit:risk for the broad relapsed-MM population the applicant proposed.
linkages.change: FDA did not approve the broad proposed indication; instead it granted accelerated approval restricted to a more heavily pretreated population (patients who had received at least 2 prior regimens including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent).

concern_quote.quote: concerns with the toxicity and uncertain magnitude of PFS improvement were cited as contributing to a negative benefit:risk profile overall.

change_quote.quote: In agreement with the ODAC recommendation, the Agency is not approving FARYDAK for the broad indication for panobinostat for the treatment of all patients with relapsed MM, requested by the Applicant.

linkages.concern: A committee member questioned whether the dose and combination of agents used in Trial D2308 was ideal for maximizing benefit while minimizing toxicity.
linkages.change: FDA imposed a postmarketing requirement for a dose-finding trial evaluating the 20 mg dose against a lower dose (possibly 15 mg) before the confirmatory trial.

concern_quote.quote: One Committee member specifically questioned whether the dose and combination of agents from the trial was ideal for maximizing benefit while minimizing toxicity.

change_quote.quote: Because of the questions that remain about the correct dose of panobinostat in combination with bortezomib and dexamethasone, the Applicant should conduct a dose-finding trial that evaluates the 20 mg dose and a lower dose (possibly 15 mg) prior to initiating the confirmatory trial.

summary: FDA took panobinostat (FARYDAK) to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee on November 6, 2014, because the overall benefit:risk looked unfavorable and trial-conduct issues clouded the PFS estimate; ODAC voted 5-2 that the benefit did not outweigh the risks for the broad relapsed-MM population the applicant proposed, citing toxicity and uncertain PFS magnitude. In agreement with ODAC, FDA declined the broad indication and instead granted accelerated approval for a narrowed, more heavily pretreated population (≥2 prior regimens including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory agent), with a confirmatory trial required. A committee member's question about the dose is reflected (not explicitly linked) in a postmarketing dose-finding requirement comparing 20 mg with a lower dose.
